title: Tell the dashboard what a host link is doing

blocks.text: The operations dashboard shows one line per host link, and the people on call act on it: UP means leave it alone, DOWN means call the network team, NO_ANSWER means call the host's support desk, and NOT_DEPLOYED means our own deployment is broken. Last month it said UP for an hour while every payment failed, and the month before it sent the network team after a host that was simply slow.

`LinkStatus.check()` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/LinkStatus.java` runs every few seconds for as long as the application runs. Q2 deploys the link's multiplexer when it starts and replaces it whenever someone edits its file in `deploy/`. `check()` and `echo()` are written. Finish the two methods marked `TODO`:

items: `probe(mux)`: what the link behind it is doing.

blocks.text: The tests deploy a real QMUX under the link's name, the way Q2 does, with a stand-in for the channel adaptor and a host behind it. Some of them redeploy it between two checks.

cases.says: a deployed, connected link whose host answers one 0800 echo is UP
a link Q2 has never deployed is NOT_DEPLOYED
when the host receives the echo and never answers, the request returns null and the link is NO_ANSWER, not UP
when the link is down the probe reports DOWN at once and leaves no echo waiting to go out when the link returns
a multiplexer deployed after the probe was created is found by the next check
after Q2 replaces the multiplexer, the next checks use the new one and the link stays UP

origin.section: 1.5.1 Spot the Problem: The Cached Multiplexer

concepts: Code finds the multiplexer by name in the JVM that runs Q2 each time it uses it; a kept reference stops receiving answers after a redeploy.
request returns null when no answer comes in time, and on a dead link it queues the message and waits, so a client checks isConnected() first to tell a down link from a silent host.
Q2 creates, starts and stops the client's components from the files in deploy/, in file-name order, and replaces a component with a new object when its file changes.
